I will keep my land in the winter wheat-summer maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. I know this system matches our climate, my machinery access, and the local market, and it spreads labor across the year in a way I can manage well. Because I am educated and I want stable returns more than unnecessary risk, I will use strong improved or hybrid seed, base fertilization on a balanced plan instead of pushing only nitrogen, and rely on a few timely irrigations rather than wasting water. For winter wheat, I will focus on good stand establishment, one strong topdressing period, careful water at the key stages, and tight disease control if pressure appears. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize with no-tillage direct seeding to save moisture and time, then push management at seedling and jointing stages so the crop closes canopy fast and holds yield in the summer heat. I am not choosing a more diversified plan this year because I would rather protect output, simplify management, and stay with the rotation I trust most on this land.
